entities.summary: brown dwarf is an astronomical object type that originated in the field of astrophysics during the Classical era. It is a celestial body that is too small to sustain nuclear fusion in its core, resulting in a surface temperature of around 300-350 K. Brown dwarfs are often considered failed stars, as they do not have enough mass to ignite fusion reactions in their cores. They are typically composed of hydrogen and helium gases, and their atmospheres can be quite different from those of planets. Brown dwarfs are of great interest to astronomers because they can provide insights into the formation and evolution of planetary systems. For example, the discovery of brown dwarfs has helped scientists understand the role of brown dwarf stars in the formation of planetary systems. They are also important for studying the properties of planetary atmospheres and the potential for life beyond Earth.
